key_insight: CURVE introduces a high-quality, human-annotated benchmark that evaluates long-video reasoning across diverse cultures and languages, revealing and addressing Western/English evaluation bias in current video models.
problem_solved: Current long-video benchmarks are Western-centric and English-dominated, failing to test cultural context, multilingual understanding, and long-range temporal reasoning needed for globally robust video models.
method: Curate a diverse corpus of long-form videos spanning multiple regions, cultures, and languages with balanced representation.
Create entirely human-generated annotations (QA, temporal reasoning, cultural-context questions) and multilingual labels/translations to require cultural and long-range reasoning.
Define standardized evaluation tasks and report baseline results to surface performance gaps across cultural and language axes.
impact: Provides practitioners a rigorous, culturally-aware evaluation suite to diagnose and improve model performance on multilingual and culturally grounded long-video reasoning, promoting fairer and more globally applicable video AI.
visual_elements: World map heatmap showing video count and language distribution by region
Timeline/strip of sampled long-video frames illustrating temporal questions and required reasoning span
Side-by-side example: video frame sequence + multilingual question + correct answer to show annotation style
Bar chart comparing baseline model performance across regions/languages to highlight bias gaps
paper_title: CURVE: A Benchmark for Cultural and Multilingual Long Video Reasoning
paper_authors: Darshan Singh, Arsha Nagrani, Kawshik Manikantan, Harman Singh, Dinesh Tewari
